system: You are a security investigator reviewing an alert. Base every claim only on the evidence available to you. Cite the record IDs that support each observation.

supporting_observations.claim: The large transfer is consistent with the approved backup activity: FILE-NWD-01 ran the inventoried StratoSafe executable as svc-archive against ingest.stratosafe-backup.com, and proxy/Zeek records show about 640 MB sent to that destination.

A Kerberos service-ticket event for svc-archive targeting FILE-NWD-01$ records a source IP of 139.162.174.124, an external address inconsistent with the stated absence of VPN and remote-administration practice.

nora.blake, identified as help desk rather than an administrator, established an RDP session to FILE-NWD-01; the successful type-10 logon came from WS-NBLAKE-01, contrary to the stated practice that remote administration is only from WS-SOKAFOR-01.

A SYSTEM PowerShell process explicitly used svc-archive credentials against DC-NWD-01, and shortly afterward DC-NWD-01 recorded a successful network logon for sam.okafor from FILE-NWD-01 using NTLM. This credential use and cross-host authentication are suspicious in context.
The evidence supports a malicious-activity finding for the surrounding access and credential-use activity, but does not establish that the observed backup transfer itself was unauthorized.

known_telemetry_limitations: The bulk transfer is recorded as an HTTPS CONNECT tunnel; the proxy logs a peek/tunnel and an inspected GET, but the provided records do not expose the transferred payload contents. Records: T040-00199, T040-00200, T040-00201, T040-00204.
The provided records do not attribute the external-IP Kerberos ticket event to a specific process or establish what client used that address. Record: T040-00193.
The supplied evidence does not include the contents of the PowerShell script, backup job manifest, or files included in the transfer.
claims_not_established: Whether the 640 MB consisted solely of expected backup data or included unauthorized data.
Whether the external-IP ticket event was attacker activity, and whether it is causally related to the local svc-archive backup process.
Why the SYSTEM PowerShell process used svc-archive credentials, and whether the subsequent sam.okafor network logon was authorized.
Whether nora.blake's RDP session involved malicious actions or was an unauthorized but benign policy violation.
additional_evidence_needed: StratoSafe job logs and manifests, including source files, destination object names, and confirmation that the transfer was expected.
Proxy and TLS inspection details, plus endpoint network/process telemetry, to correlate the external ticket event and transfer with originating processes or sessions.
Domain-controller authentication details and network/device attribution for the 139.162.174.124 ticket event.
The contents and execution history of C:\Scripts\certificate-health.ps1, and relevant credential-use or secret-access audit records.
RDP session activity for nora.blake on FILE-NWD-01, including commands, file access, and session authorization.
